result:
I fixed 12 rules in `pricebook.py`. A check script read each rule's docstring and compared it with the function's output over many quantity and unit-price combinations. After the fixes, all 150 rules match.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 19, 40 | Applied from 11 units, but the docstring says 10+ | Changed the threshold to `qty >= 10` |
| 21, 52, 144 | Capped the price (`min(base, 30000)`) instead of the discount | Calculate the discount, then cap it |
| 51, 53 | Rounded with `round()` instead of flooring to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 74 | Docstring says whole, but the code discounted only units above the threshold | Discount the whole order |
| 136, 145 | Docstring says marginal, but the code discounted the whole order | Discount only units above the threshold |
| 118 | Applied the 30,000 won cap only when the discount was over 60,000 | Always cap at 30,000 won |
| 67 | Used `qty >= 31` instead of 30+ | Changed to `qty >= 30`. At exactly 30 units the marginal discount is 0 either way, so prices don't change; this just makes it match the docstring |

STATUS: DONE
